UEFA Women’s Champions League zine collaborates with art duo Swedish Girls to bring fandom to the streets of Gothenburg
items.description: Queenzine is a fanzine that celebrates iconic figures in the UEFA Women’s Champions League and the fans that add fuel to their fire. To mark it’s most recent issue, physical copies of the mag sat in various cultural spots in Gothenburg, on custom stands made by one of Sweden’s most exciting art duos.

items.title: Vucko’s motion identity for Etsy is built on joy, simplicity and craft
items.description: The studio’s motion design work for the online marketplace solidifies Etsy’s identity while providing it with the capacity to adapt to each department’s specific needs.

items.title: Georgie McAusland on refusing expensive tools to get more “squish and texture” into her drawings
items.description: The artist is finding joy through drawing on location, capturing the true atmosphere of everyday scenes.

items.title: Dum Dum Studio’s inventive design emerges from an open mind and a love of play
items.description: Whether it’s an identity, custom typeface or art direction, this studio is sourcing inspiration from the history of it’s home city, Monterrey – the industrial capital of Mexico.

items.title: Why the retro brand identities of Biabum studio have illustration built into their DNA
items.description: The Brazilian studio has a knack for finding the right colour palette to create something that will move people.

items.title: Missing summer? Dive into Emily Stein colourful and chaotic snaps of Italian waterparks
items.description: The photographer captures the retro aesthetics and loud, lurid nature of every kid’s dream day out: “A waterpark is summer turned up to full volume.”

items.title: Adobe Max Miami 2026 goes live online
items.description: Adobe’s creativity conference returns on 10-11 November, with a free online pass and a roster that runs from Terry Crews to Adobe’s incoming CEO.

items.title: Trade Secrets: a free webinar series reveals the photography techniques behind Ana Flores, Sam Nicklin and Arielle Bobb-Willis photographs
items.description: In partnership with MPB, we’re launching Trade Secrets – a three-part webinar series exploring the ideas, techniques and kit behind great photography, with practical advice from three of our favourite image-makers.

items.title: Nicer Tuesdays London: Get tickets for Studio Feixen, Oscar Hudson, Fiona Quadri and Adam Lin in December!
items.description: For our final event of the year, you can expect a feast of talks on playful typography systems, subversive cinema, public art and intimate photography from four fabulous creatives.

items.title: James Barnett and Poppy French document the eccentricities of Britain with warmth and humour
items.description: For a new documentary series on It’s Nice That, the creative duo set about finding niche subcultures and communities around the UK and the characters at the heart of them. We chat to the content creator and photographer about their approach and discoveries.

items.title: “Strong and sporty”: Nymzo is the trendy chess brand designed for a new wave of players
items.description: Over the past few years chess changed – it caught the cool factor. But, the gear was at a stalemate. Here’s where Nymzo founders Elliott Walker and Tim Hucklesby enter the picture.

items.title: Decoding 22, A Million: Eric Timothy Carlson on carving Bon Iver’s iconic visual universe ten years later
items.description: Bon Iver’s esoteric and mysterious music spills out into it’s album cover in clusters of meaningful symbols, all thanks to this designer.

items.title: “You will always be a designer, whether that’s full time or not”
items.description: It’s not the same world as it used to be. Leave university, get a job and stay in that job for forty years. It’s also not the same as a mere five years ago, where you leave university, get a job and stay in that job for three years before moving on to another either. Creatives are forming uniquely shaped practices of their own design, consisting of multiple avenues. But what if we’re stretching ourselves too thin? items.title: Elizabeth Goodspeed on the impossible economics of art education in the US
items.description: American art schools are closing even as tuition fees reach extraordinary heights, with new funding cuts set to make attendance even less attainable for many would-be students. But if an art education is worth more than the salary it produces, why have we accepted that only those who can afford it should get one?

items.title: Mona Chalabi’s illustrated book about wealth inequality will make you talk to your friends about money
items.description: Think you’re not a ‘numbers person’? The Pulitzer Prize-winning illustrator and journalist Mona Chalabi wants you to think again. On the release of her new book, Ten Lives, she chats about how pictures have the power to make economics accessible.

items.title: Starting a creative career has never felt harder – 28 industry voices on what comes next
